blocks.prompt: 12. Find the equations of the circles of radius 5 that are tangent to the line \(4x + 3y - 10 = 0\) at the point \((1, 2)\).
blocks.explanation:
Radius and point of contact are given; the centre is 5 units from \((1, 2)\) along the normal.
We need the equations; one circle on each side of the line.
Plan: centre on the normal at \((1, 2)\) with \(|CP| = 5\).
steps:
Given: radius 5; tangent \(4x + 3y - 10 = 0\) at \(P(1, 2)\).
To find: the equations of the circles.
Method: The centre \(C(h, k)\) lies on the normal at \(P\), and \(|CP| = 5\).

Normal at \((1, 2)\)
\[4x + 3y - 10 = 0 \Rightarrow m = -\tfrac{4}{3}\]
\[y - 2 = \tfrac{3}{4}(x - 1)\]
\[3x - 4y + 5 = 0\]
Why: \((1, 2)\) is on the line (\(4 + 6 - 10 = 0\)); the normal slope is \(\frac{3}{4}\).

Centre on the normal
\[k - 2 = \tfrac{3}{4}(h - 1)\]
Why: \(C\) satisfies the normal.

Check
\[\dfrac{|20 + 15 - 10|}{5} = 5,\quad \dfrac{|-12 - 3 - 10|}{5} = 5\]
Why: Both centres are 5 units from the line; \((1, 2)\) is the midpoint of the two centres.
